Mixture model with mixed indicator types

mixture.Rd

Fits a latent class (mixture) model whose indicators are of several types in one model: categorical (binary or polytomous), continuous (normal) and counts (Poisson, negative binomial, zero-inflated Poisson), estimated by maximum likelihood with Mplus-style random starts. Indicators are independent within class (local independence across and within types).

Usage

mixture(
  data,
  K,
  categorical = NULL,
  continuous = NULL,
  count = NULL,
  negbin = NULL,
  zip = NULL,
  variances = "equal",
  dispersion = "equal",
  inflation = "equal",
  starts = c(100, 20),
  covariates = NULL,
  ref = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  cluster = NULL,
  strata = NULL,
  start = NULL,
  optseed = NULL,
  seed = 20261119,
  maxiter = 5000,
  tol = 1e-10,
  polish = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

Data frame or matrix (one row per respondent). Indicators may be factors, characters, logicals, labelled vectors or numeric category codes; NA marks a missing response.

K

Number of classes (a positive whole number).

categorical, continuous, count, negbin, zip

Indicator columns of each type (tidyselect): categorical; continuous (normal); Poisson counts; negative binomial counts; zero-inflated Poisson counts.

variances

Within-class variances of the continuous indicators: "equal" across classes (default, Mplus) or "varying".

dispersion

Negative binomial dispersions: "equal" across classes (default, Mplus) or "varying".

inflation

Zero-inflation probabilities: "equal" across classes (default, Mplus) or "varying".

starts

Length-2 integer vector: number of stage-1 random starts and of stage-2 starts iterated to convergence (Mplus STARTS). A single number is recycled. The default c(100, 20) with 20 stage-1 EM iterations corresponds to Mplus STARTS = 100 20; STITERATIONS = 20 (the Mplus defaults are 20 4 and 10 iterations).

covariates

Optional numeric covariates for a one-step latent class regression (Mplus c ON x): columns of data (tidyselect, e.g. c(age, female)) or a numeric data frame / matrix with one row per row of data. Needs K >= 2.

ref

Reference class of the latent class regression (default: the last class).

weights

Optional sampling weights: one column of data (e.g. w) or a numeric vector with one value per row; rescaled to sum to the number of analysed rows.

cluster

Optional primary sampling units (PSUs) of a complex survey design (Mplus CLUSTER with TYPE = COMPLEX): one column of data (e.g. psu) or a vector with one value per row. Standard errors, the MLR scaling correction factor and the tests built on them (compare_models(), Wald tests of r3step(), bch(), dcat()) are then design-based: computed from PSU totals of the weighted scores. Estimates and the log-likelihood do not change. blrt() is not available (as in Mplus). Analysed rows may not have a missing value.

strata

Optional strata of the design (Mplus STRATIFICATION): one column of data or a vector. PSUs are nested in strata (equal cluster codes in different strata are different PSUs); without cluster every row is its own PSU. A stratum with a single PSU is kept, as in Mplus.

start

Optional start values: a fitted latentmix model of the same type and number of classes (for example a fit to other data, or with fewer random starts). EM then runs from its estimates only, without random starts (Mplus user starting values with STARTS = 0; the analogue of OUTPUT: SVALUES).

optseed

Optional start number: rerun only that random start (stage 1 and stage 2), the analogue of Mplus OPTSEED; see refit_start().

seed

Random seed for the random starts.

maxiter

Maximum number of EM iterations in stage 2.

tol

Convergence tolerance: change in the log-likelihood per case.

polish

TRUE (default): after EM converges, finish the best solution by Newton–Raphson with analytic derivatives, as Mplus switches from EM to quasi-Newton, and keep the result when it raises the log-likelihood and lowers the gradient. EM's stopping rule can leave weakly determined parameters short of the maximum (they then differ from Mplus in the third decimal); estimates, log-likelihood, posteriors and standard errors are then those of the maximum. FALSE reports the EM solution. After a GPU fit the polish runs on the CPU. Two-level models are always finished by Newton steps, so polish has no effect there.

Value

An object of class latentmix (see lca()) with info$kind == "MIXED" and the extra component types (the type of every indicator, in the order of names: categorical, continuous, Poisson, negative binomial, zero-inflated).

Details

Indicators. Choose the columns of every type with tidyselect syntax (starts_with("ace_"), c(sleep, stress), "depress"); give at least one type, and list a column under one type only. Categorical indicators may be factors, characters, logicals or numeric codes (as in lca()); continuous and count indicators must be numeric, counts non-negative whole numbers. Missing values (NA) are handled by full-information maximum likelihood; rows with every indicator missing are not analysed.

Count models (log link, class-specific means), as Mplus COUNT:

argumentmodelMplusclass-specific parameters
countPoissonu (p)log rate
negbinnegative binomial (NB2, Var = mu + alpha mu^2)u (nb)log mean; dispersion alpha if dispersion = "varying"
zipzero-inflated Poissonu (pi)log rate; inflation logit if inflation = "varying"

By default (as in Mplus) continuous variances, negative binomial dispersions and zero-inflation probabilities are equal across classes.

Parameters (parameters()) are on Mplus's scales: probabilities and thresholds, means and variances (original scale), "log mean" (Mplus "Means" of a count variable), "dispersion" and "inflation logit" (Mplus u#1). countparams() gives the count parameters on the natural scale; itemprobs() the categorical and profilemeans() / profilevariances() the continuous indicators. Covariates, weights, starts and the three-step functions (r3step(), bch(), dcat()) work as for lca(); lmr() and blrt() are available. cluster and strata give design-based standard errors (Mplus TYPE = MIXTURE COMPLEX), as in lca(). start (a fitted mixture() model with the same indicators) runs EM from its estimates only; optseed reruns a single random start (refit_start()).

References

Muthén, B., & Shedden, K. (1999). Finite mixture modeling with mixture outcomes using the EM algorithm. Biometrics, 55(2), 463–469. doi:10.1111/j.0006-341X.1999.00463.x

Lambert, D. (1992). Zero-inflated Poisson regression, with an application to defects in manufacturing. Technometrics, 34(1), 1–14. doi:10.2307/1269547

Hilbe, J. M. (2011). Negative Binomial Regression (2nd ed.). Cambridge University Press. doi:10.1017/CBO9780511973420

Muthén, L. K., & Muthén, B. O. (1998–2017). Mplus User's Guide (8th ed.). Muthén & Muthén.

See also

countparams(), lca(), lpa(), parameters(), classify().

Examples

data(aces)
# \donttest{
# ACE classes with the depressive-symptom score as an overdispersed count indicator
m <- mixture(aces, K = 4, categorical = starts_with("ace_"), negbin = depress)
#> Starting Julia ...
m
#> ━━ Mixture model with mixed indicators ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

# all three types: major depression by 21 (binary), symptom scores (continuous) and the
# number of adverse childhood experiences (Poisson count), with one-step covariates
data(depression)
p <- mixture(depression, K = 2, categorical = mde21, continuous = c(dep1, anx1, distress21),
             count = aces, covariates = c(female, low_ses))
coeftable(p)
